chunks: And your Lord knows whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others, and We gave David the Psalms.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of some prophets being preferred over others in Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse establishes the principle of 'Tafḍīl' (preferment) among the Prophets, affirming that while all are infallible, their stations vary according to divine wisdom, with Prophet Dawud’s receipt of the Zabur serving as a specific example of this hierarchy. This distinction is often linked to the unique spiritual and political authority granted to certain prophets, foreshadowing the elevated status of the Ahl al-Bayt in later Shia theology. The verse thus balances the universal dignity of prophethood with the nuanced gradations of divine favor.
